alloys.alloys_notes: Table 1 reports the chemical composition of the tested steel in wt.%, with Fe as balance. The high Al content (>4 wt%) is claimed to expand the δ-ferrite phase region and reduce density (~1.3 % weight reduction per 1 wt% Al). Steel fabricated via vacuum induction melting (VIM).
alloys.description: A low-density δ-ferrite steel fabricated via vacuum induction melting (VIM), designed with high Al content (~4.5 wt%) to reduce density while using a lamellar microstructure design to overcome the inherently poor toughness of coarse δ-ferrite.

source.reason: Table 1 gives the chemical composition of the single tested steel (C 0.35, Si 0.26, Mn 1.47, Al 4.50, Cr 0.26, Mo 0.28, Ni 1.47, Fe Bal, wt.%), and the text identifies it as a low-density δ-ferrite steel fabricated via VIM; only one alloy composition is studied in the whole paper.

paper.paper_scope: Systematically investigates how rolling temperature (low-temperature zone 650–750 °C vs high-temperature zone 850–950 °C) controls microstructural evolution (ultra-fine spheroidized carbide/ferrite composite lamellae vs honeycomb martensite lamellae with equiaxed DIF grains) and thereby the impact fracture toughness and strength–plasticity synergy of a low-density δ-ferrite steel.
paper.title: Enabling superior impact toughness of low-density δ-ferrite steel by dispersing ultra-fine spheroidized carbides in the ferrite/carbide composite lamellae

aliases: hot-forged experimental steel prior to rolling
processes.description: Steel ingot homogenized at 1200 °C for 4 h, then hot forged to a thickness of 40 mm and air cooled to room temperature; microstructure shows no obvious lamellae, mainly coarse δ-ferrite with M/A (martensite/austenite) constituents.
processes.process_name: homogenization + hot forging + air cooling (pre-rolling state)
processes.processes_notes: This is the precursor/control state of the tested steel prior to any rolling; it serves as parent for the four rolled conditions.

source.reason: The paper states the ingot was homogenized at 1200 °C for 4 h, hot forged to 40 mm and air cooled, and Fig. 3a–c characterize this hot-forged steel before rolling as a control group.

processes.description: Hot-forged plate reheated to 650 °C and held 2 h, then hot rolled with 60 % reduction (40 mm → 16 mm) and air cooled to room temperature; produces alternating δ-ferrite lamellae and ultra-fine spherical carbide/ferrite composite lamellae (carbide ~158.3 ± 76.9 nm, density 1.7 ± 0.2 μm⁻²).
processes.process_name: low-temperature hot rolling at 650 °C + air cooling
processes.processes_notes: Belongs to the low-temperature rolling zone (650–750 °C) where carbides precipitate and lamellar δ-F + C/F structure forms.

source.reason: Text states specimens were heated to 650 °C (or 750/850/950 °C), held for 2 h, then hot rolled with 60 % reduction from 40 mm to 16 mm and air cooled, giving four groups named R650, R750, R850 and R950.

processes.description: Hot-forged plate reheated to 750 °C and held 2 h, then hot rolled with 60 % reduction (40 mm → 16 mm) and air cooled to room temperature; similar lamellar δ-F + C/F structure but coarser carbides (~247.3 ± 86.8 nm, density 0.6 ± 0.1 μm⁻²) due to Ostwald ripening.
processes.process_name: low-temperature hot rolling at 750 °C + air cooling
processes.processes_notes: Belongs to the low-temperature rolling zone (650–750 °C), above the carbide-stability range of the R650 condition.

source.reason: Text states specimens were heated to 650/750/850/950 °C, held for 2 h, hot rolled with 60 % reduction, air cooled, and named R650/R750/R850/R950; R750 shows carbide coarsening.

processes.description: Hot-forged plate reheated to 850 °C and held 2 h, then hot rolled with 60 % reduction (40 mm → 16 mm) and air cooled; carbides fully dissolved, forming a duplex structure of δ-ferrite lamellae and honeycomb martensite lamellae containing equiaxed DIF grains (M 33.2 vol%, δ-F 66.8 vol%).
processes.process_name: high-temperature hot rolling at 850 °C + air cooling
processes.processes_notes: Belongs to the high-temperature rolling zone (850–950 °C) where DRX and DIFT occur and carbides dissolve.

source.reason: Text states specimens were heated to 850 °C, held 2 h, hot rolled with 60 % reduction and air cooled, giving the R850 condition with a duplex δ-ferrite + honeycomb martensite structure.

processes.description: Hot-forged plate reheated to 950 °C and held 2 h, then hot rolled with 60 % reduction (40 mm → 16 mm) and air cooled; duplex δ-ferrite + honeycomb martensite structure with larger equiaxed DIF grains (M 59.0 vol%, δ-F 41.0 vol%).
processes.process_name: high-temperature hot rolling at 950 °C + air cooling
processes.processes_notes: Belongs to the high-temperature rolling zone (850–950 °C); higher temperature increases the honeycomb martensite fraction and DIF grain size.

source.reason: Text states specimens were heated to 950 °C, held 2 h, hot rolled with 60 % reduction and air cooled, giving the R950 condition with increased honeycomb martensite proportion.

aliases: hot-forged experimental steel prior to rolling

source.reason: The hot-forged, air-cooled tested steel prior to rolling is explicitly characterized as the control state (Fig. 3a–c); it combines the single alloy composition with the pre-rolling process.
R650 is the tested steel rolled at 650 °C with 60 % reduction then air cooled, characterized by impact energy 207.5 J and ultra-fine spherical carbides (~158.3 nm).
R750 is the tested steel rolled at 750 °C with 60 % reduction then air cooled, with coarser carbides and lower impact energy (75.9 J).
R850 is the tested steel rolled at 850 °C with 60 % reduction then air cooled, showing a duplex δ-ferrite + honeycomb martensite structure and low impact energy (5.6 J).
R950 is the tested steel rolled at 950 °C with 60 % reduction then air cooled, with the highest martensite fraction and lowest impact energy (4.6 J).

unmapped_findings: Carbides in the R650 steel were identified by TEM/SAED and EDS as various types including MC, M23C6 and M7C3, mainly concentrated outside the δ-ferrite lamellae as products of martensite decomposition and element (C, Cr, Mn) enrichment.

Mechanical characterization was performed by room-temperature tensile tests (rod-shaped specimens, 25 mm gauge length) and Charpy V-notch impact tests (10 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm, notch on rolled surface, impact direction perpendicular to RD); microstructural techniques included SEM/EBSD (RD-ND plane), nanoindentation (5 mN peak load) and TEM/HRTEM.
